summary.name: RustCast
summary.one_liner: RustCast is a free, open-source keyboard-first app launcher for macOS that searches installed apps, files, clipboard history, and runs custom shell-script modes.
use_cases: quickly open installed apps without the mouse
switch work contexts with one keypress
run shell scripts or dev servers from a hotkey
trigger launcher actions from scripts or Shortcuts
summary.what_it_does: RustCast is a macOS launcher that searches and opens installed apps via a global hotkey. It includes inline expression evaluation, unit conversion, emoji search, and a Google search shortcut that appends "?" to a query. A clipboard history is available from its own keyboard shortcut, and file search is supported. Modes let users map a key to any shell script, such as presentation, dev, or focus setups. Configuration lives in a single TOML file covering hotkeys, aliases, search engine, and theme. A rustcast:// URL scheme (v0.7.4+) allows opening apps or showing and quitting the launcher from scripts.
notable: Modes run arbitrary shell scripts from a single keypress
Configured through one TOML file with hotkeys, aliases, and theme settings
rustcast:// URL scheme for scripting and automation
Installable via Homebrew cask, DMG from GitHub Releases, or cargo install
caveats: Only macOS is named on the page
Sponsorship is optional; the page describes the project as free forever
